title: Safe handling and staged work zones
audience: Coordinators, support workers and trained cleaners who may be asked to work in a home affected by hoarding or environmental neglect, as part of an authorised support plan. Not a qualification or authority to clear a property, dispose of a resident's belongings, enter by force, or provide welfare or clinical support.
learningOutcomes: Set a work zone, its boundary and an order of work with the resident.
Separate items into four labelled categories and keep the traffic route clear.
Reconcile the daily inventory with the item-decision log.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers planning and handling limits in a staged job. It does not set numerical lifting limits, which come from the employer's plan and manual-handling controls, and it does not authorise the removal of possessions.

instruction.heading: Small, agreed zones
instruction.body: Controlled work in small, named zones reduces re-accumulation, manual-handling strain and the loss of items the resident values. Agree the zones with the resident, one room or one area at a time. Set a work and rest pattern, the lifting limits from the plan and a daily inventory review. A crew that rushes several rooms at once and mixes keepsakes with waste has breached the agreed plan.

instruction.heading: Four labelled categories and a clear route
instruction.body: Keep items the resident is keeping, items for relocation, undecided items and items for authorised disposal in four separate, labelled zones. Keep the traffic route clear and separate from the staging zones. Handle each item once and move it to its labelled zone. If a category is unclear, the item moves to the undecided zone, not the disposal zone. The daily review confirms that the zones still match the item-decision log, and it records any change and the reason for it.

procedure: Agree the zone, its boundary and its order of work with the resident before starting.
Set the work and rest pattern and the lifting limit from the plan.
Label four zones: retain, relocate, undecided and authorised disposal.
Keep the traffic route clear, and do not stage items in it.
Review the inventory at the end of each day, and reconcile it with the item-decision log.
Stop and restore the separation if keepsakes are mixed with waste, and audit the change with the resident.

workedExamples.situation: A crew rushes several rooms at once and mixes keepsakes with waste.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the process. Restore the separation of clean and dirty items, and audit the unapproved change with the resident. Return to one agreed zone at a time.

workedExamples.situation: A heavy box of papers is found in a bedroom, and the plan sets a lifting limit.
workedExamples.reasoning: Only within the plan's lifting limit, with a second person or lifting aid where the plan requires. Otherwise leave it in place and record it for a decision.

equipmentAndPpe: Lifting aids and the lifting limits set in the plan.
Four labelled zone markers and barrier tape for the boundary.
Daily inventory sheet. No real belongings are moved in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Clearing several rooms at once to finish faster.
commonErrors.prevention: Work one agreed zone at a time, with a daily review.

commonErrors.error: Placing undecided items in the disposal zone.
commonErrors.prevention: Undecided items go to the undecided zone and stay there until the resident decides.

commonErrors.error: Lifting heavy loads beyond the plan's limit.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the agreed limit, the lifting aids and a second person where the plan requires.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Lifting limits and work patterns come from the plan and the employer's manual-handling controls. This lesson does not set numerical lifting limits.
Work in a home with unknown materials, sharps or unstable stacks stops under the other lessons in this module, whatever the zone plan says.

qualityStandard: The learner sets a zone, a boundary and an order of work with the resident.
The learner separates items into four labelled categories and keeps the traffic route clear.
The learner reconciles the daily inventory with the decision log.
documentationEvidence: Zone plan with boundaries and the order of work agreed with the resident.
Daily inventory review, reconciled with the item-decision log.
Audit record for any unapproved change.
summary: Work one agreed zone at a time.
Keep four categories separate, and undecided items stay undecided.
Lift only within the plan's limits.

knowledgeChecks.question: A crew wants to clear three rooms at once. What is the best approach?
options: Work one agreed zone at a time, with a daily review.
Clear all three, because it is faster.
Clear the rooms at night when the resident is asleep.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should an item the resident has not yet decided about be placed?
options: In the undecided zone, until the resident decides.

knowledgeChecks.question: A box is too heavy to lift safely under the plan. What should happen?
options: Lift it quickly with a twist to save time.
Drop it into the disposal zone.
Use the agreed limit, the lifting aid or a second person where the plan requires, or leave it and record it.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a home by force, to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings without valid consent, to handle or dispose of hazardous waste, to deal with unstable stacks or structural hazards, or to provide welfare, clinical or safeguarding assessments. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Work is done only under an authorised support plan and a written agreement with the resident, within the limits set by the employer and the local law. Tenancy, safeguarding and information-sharing rights are jurisdiction-specific, and fire-risk, structural, pest and hazardous-waste decisions belong to the competent authorities and specialists named in the plan. Where authority or consent is unclear, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: consent is not specific, documented and current; the resident has objected or withdrawn consent; a party seeks entry by force, nonconsensual disposal or removal of personal documents; a fire-load, ignition, egress or obstruction hazard is present; a stack or structure is unstable; pests, unknown liquids or mouldy goods are present; sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are found; waste would go to general disposal without characterisation; private information is requested without authority; or the work would go beyond the approved plan. Stopping is a valid professional outcome. Record the disagreement, protect the resident's choices and refer the authority dispute before any property is moved.
